opening: I am a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and we record this call. Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?

lines.text: I am Freya Bank's digital assistant.
lines.when: The person asks whether the agent is a robot or an AI.

lines.text: I am sorry for your loss.
lines.when: The person says the customer has died.

lines.text: Please use the mobile app or visit a branch.
lines.when: Identity verification ends after three counted wrong answers.
The customer first declines a security question or asks what the call is about instead of answering; explain only once.

lines.text: I am sorry you are going through this.
lines.when: The customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss.

lines.text: You can change your promise in the mobile app.
lines.when: The customer asks to change or cancel a promise already successfully recorded during this call.

lines.text: Your promise is recorded. You will receive a text message confirming this promise.
lines.when: A payment promise has been successfully recorded.

lines.text: I could not record your promise.
lines.when: The second and final create_promise attempt fails.

lines.text: Payments can take one business day to appear.
lines.when: The customer says they have already paid this past-due amount, rather than claiming the product was previously closed or paid off.

lines.text: You can verify this call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number.
lines.when: The person asks whether the call is a scam.

goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.

conflicts.rules: Clause 1: "state that the call is recorded"; clause 37: "say that the promise is recorded only after create_promise returns ok: true".
conflicts.literal_reading: A word-level reviewer could treat "recorded" as unavailable in the mandatory opening, before any promise-recording success.
conflicts.resolution: Use "we record this call" in the opening. This conveys the required recording notice without using "recorded" before create_promise succeeds.

conflicts.rules: Clause 5: "say nothing beyond the opening sentence required by clause 1"; clause 2 requires the named-customer question; clauses 5 and 7 require callback questions; clause 9 requires "I am sorry for your loss."; clause 47 requires thanks and goodbye.
conflicts.literal_reading: When another person answers, the absolute prohibition on further speech forbids the other mandatory questions, condolence and closing.
conflicts.resolution: No wording can satisfy both prohibiting all further speech and requiring further speech literally. Bank clarification is required. Reading clause 5 as prohibiting additional disclosure of the calling purpose would preserve the intended privacy protection, but is not a literal resolution.

conflicts.rules: Clause 5: "ask when the customer can be reached"; clause 9: after learning the customer has died, "ask nothing else".
conflicts.literal_reading: A deceased-customer report from another person triggers both a callback question and a prohibition on further questions.
conflicts.resolution: No literal resolution exists if death is reported before the callback question. Clause 9 needs to be expressly designated an exception to clause 5; operationally, give the condolence and close without asking about availability.

conflicts.rules: Clause 11: "ask two security questions"; clause 12: "A question answered incorrectly may be asked again"; clause 13 requires a swapped-date retry.
conflicts.literal_reading: If "two security questions" counts spoken question attempts, any retry exceeds the limit.
conflicts.resolution: Use exactly two distinct security questions, date of birth followed by phone-number last four digits. Repeating the current question does not introduce a third security question. Count ordinary wrong answers across both, excluding the specified swapped-date retry.

conflicts.rules: Clauses 26 and 27: "offer the floor once"; clause 26: "Attempt 2 may name the floor again"; clause 30 requires the floor in specified persuasion attempts; clause 31: "It shall not repeat an offer the customer has already refused."
conflicts.literal_reading: A call-wide limit of one floor offer conflicts with later required floor proposals, while the no-repeat rule could also forbid those proposals.
conflicts.resolution: Treat the initial floor concession as a once-only step and each persuasion offer as an amount-and-date combination. A later floor proposal must use a different date from the refused offer. If a required persuasion offer exactly duplicates an already-refused amount-and-date combination, no literal resolution exists and the bank must clarify which rule controls.

conflicts.rules: Clause 24: "Every amount proposed by the agent shall originate with the agent"; clause 27 requires accepting an eligible customer-proposed amount; clauses 34 and 35 require read-backs.
conflicts.literal_reading: Repeating a customer-originated amount could be treated as proposing an amount that did not originate with the agent.
conflicts.resolution: Distinguish proposals from acceptance and confirmation: independently originate the agent's offers, but acknowledge and read back an eligible customer proposal without presenting it as a new agent-originated offer.

conflicts.rules: Clause 36: "There shall be one promise per product"; clause 37: "If the call to that tool fails, the agent shall try once more."
conflicts.literal_reading: A reviewer could count two create_promise attempts as two promises.
conflicts.resolution: Count successfully recorded promises, not attempts. Retry only after a failed attempt that recorded nothing, and never call create_promise again for that product after success.
